text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT: AP-SOUTHEAST-2 partial networking + ELB 5xx increase. Pager triggered (severity: P1). Thread started.

mira (oncall-sre): hitting 502/504s for inference/stream endpoints from APAC customers. dashboards show ELB backend unhealthy counts spiking.

carla (support): multiple customer tickets reporting degraded responses and timeouts, high severity. Customer-impact: paid customers in APAC seeing ~30-60% error rate for some endpoints.

mira (oncall-sre): checking quick metrics — increased 5xx on redwood-model-apse2-elb, target group health shows 20% unhealthy. Route53 health checks for regional records returning >50% failed for ap-southeast-2.

lee (netops): seeing BGP egress asymmetry in ap-southeast-2 AZb, some edge nodes reporting packet loss to AWS NAT gateways. Could be AWS networking flap.

mira (oncall-sre): I ran probe curl from our runner in ap-southeast-2:
```
curl -v https://inference.apse2.redwood.ai/health
> HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
```
Backend logs show connections reset during TLS handshake, repeated ENETUNREACH in nginx.

davinder (eng-runtime): double-checking autoscaler + target instance states — autoscale healthy, instances fine at host level. No OOMs. Looks like path-level drops.

mira (oncall-sre): created AWS case 0123456789 (contacted aws-support). Starting immediate mitigations: 1) increase ELB deregistration delay to lower thrash, 2) enable fallback routing to secondary region via Route53 failover weights, 3) notify support and customers.

kai (platform): recommend we temporarily change Route53 weight to shift ~60% traffic to us-east-1 for critical routes. But note cached resolvers may keep clients pointed here.

evan (sre-manager): approve cross-region weight change. Notify sales/CS and execs. Prepare incident bridge.

mira (oncall-sre): performing weight change now. Command used in terraform console (manual edit):
```
# set weight for apse2 to 40, useast to 60
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --change-batch file://change.json --hosted-zone-id ZZZZZ
```
Applying... :hourglass:

incident-bot: [ACTION] Route53 weights updated (apse2 -> 40, us-east -> 60). Cache propagation expected ~TTL 60s-300s depending on resolver.

carla (support): let customers with open tickets know we've shifted traffic to fallback region; some may need to retry. Drafting msg.

lee (netops): AWS console shows multiple ELB edge nodes reporting increased 5xx and path errors. Support responded: "We're seeing an issue in AP-SOUTHEAST-2 AZB affecting egress to our partner peering." AWS recommended failing over.

mira (oncall-sre): traffic has dropped ~45% for apse2 on our dashboards, errors down overall. But some customers still hit 502s due to resolver caches (ISPs).

davinder (eng-runtime): enabling additional prefix caching and increasing KV cache TTL to reduce cross-region calls. Also throttling heavy streaming routes to reduce tail pressure.

mira (oncall-sre): adding a temporary rate limit rule on WAF for abnormal client patterns from edge nodes showing high retry to reduce noise.

carla (support): customer update pushed to affected users: "We're experiencing degraded responses in APAC due to an upstream cloud networking issue; we've shifted traffic to a fallback region and are monitoring. If you see issues, please retry after 5 minutes." :white_check_mark:

aws-support: AWS Support: Case 0123456789 - We are actively investigating a regional networking egress flap in ap-southeast-2 affecting ELB->NAT paths. We will update in 15 mins.

mira (oncall-sre): I'm preparing a concise impact assessment for postmortem: - Start: ~1856007000 (first alerts) - Scope: ELB 5xx increases, Route53 health checks failing, ~30-60% errors for some APAC customers - Root cause (probable): AWS regional networking egress instability impacting load balancer connections - Mitigation: Route53 weight shift, ELB adjustments, WAF throttle, cache TTL changes, autoscaler adjustments - Next: coordinate with infra eng + incident PM for RCA + customer comms.

evan (sre-manager): take ownership of incident response timeline and postmortem. Mira handoff to Davinder for follow-ups in the next shift at 1856012000.

mira (oncall-sre): handing off: I've documented current actions in incident doc and linked AWS case. Davinder, please continue until resolved.

davinder (eng-runtime): ack, taking over. I'll keep the bridge open and follow up with AWS for root cause and timeline. Planning to run additional synthetic checks across public resolvers to estimate chest of cached DNS.

lee (netops): suggest we run a DNS TTL advisory: publish a note to ops docs to reduce DNS TTL for critical endpoints during region failover windows.

carla (support): is there any customer-facing ETA?

mira (oncall-sre): short answer: monitoring; initial mitigations reduced errors but full resolution depends on AWS repair of their egress fabric. We'll update customers every 30 minutes.

aws-support: Update: we've isolated a peering fabric issue in ap-southeast-2 affecting outbound NAT path from some AZs. Mitigation underway; expected update within 30-60 mins.

davinder (eng-runtime): running a script to simulate reconnect behavior and graceful retry backoff to avoid stampeding clients. Pushing small config to streaming proxy: reduce parallel streams per connection from 8 -> 4.

mira (oncall-sre): marking current status: mitigated (partial). Severity reduced from P1 -> P2 for follow-up. Continuing monitoring.

carla (support): communicated mitigation to customers and CS. We'll aggregate impacted accounts for credits if outage persists beyond SLA thresholds.

evan (sre-manager): good work. After stabilizes, please start RCA and list follow-ups: 1) adjust failover runbook to include faster Route53 weight automation 2) improve synthetic checks for ELB egress path 3) add playbook for DNS TTL reduction during failovers 4) postmortem + customer timeline.

mira (oncall-sre): noted. Closing on-call handoff: davinder will continue monitoring and coordinate with aws-support. I'll file the incident doc and kick off postmortem template.

davinder (eng-runtime): taking over. Bridge stays open. I'll update thread with AWS findings and final timeline.

incident-bot: IncidentUpdate: Severity changed to P2 at 1856008200.

mira (oncall-sre): thanks all — great coordinated response.

davinder (eng-runtime): next update in 20m unless AWS pushes full fix earlier.

aws-support: Final: Root cause confirmed - regional egress fabric intermittent packet drops due to a faulty edge router; fully replaced and service normalized at 1856008300.

davinder (eng-runtime): AWS reports fix deployed. Metrics show errors returned to baseline. Will wait 30m to confirm no regression then start RCA.

incident-bot: IncidentResolved: AP-SOUTHEAST-2 egress issue resolved at 1856008340. Postmortem link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1856007654/postmortem

carla (support): pushing final customer update now.

mira (oncall-sre): closing thread for operational updates; leave it open for postmortem comments. Great teamwork. :pray:
